newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba sees economy picking up, jobs benefits limited.
newsitem.headline: Buba sees economy picking up, jobs benefits limited.

text.p: German economic growth is likely to gain pace after a pause in growth in the winter months, but the impact on the jobs market will be limited, the Bundesbank said on Wednesday.

In its annual report, the central bank said, "The conditions for this (a pick-up in the pace of growth) seem to be generally extremely favourable, although considerable structural problems remain which prevent a broader-based upswing."

But it added, "Even if a clear economic recovery in the course of the year should put an end to the downtrend in employment levels and replaces it with an uptrend, it is not likely that a strong fall in unemployment will result."

Favourable factors for a resumption of growth included the normalisation of the exchange rate, low interest rates and recent moderate wage increases, the Bundesbank said, adding this year's wage round also seemed likely to bring moderate rises.
While export trade was still expected to be the main growth motor, the Bundesbank expressed hope that this positive stimulus could also spread to domestic investment activity this year.

"If export business proves favourable in the long-term, then the prospects increase on the demand side for this, taken together with the favourable supply conditions and the improvement in the tax framework which it is to be hoped will soon take effect, to ignite companies' investment interest."
An increase in investment activity would also help the construction sector, whose weakness at the turn of the year was largely responsible for the sluggishness of the economy.
From the inflation side, the price-conscious central bank said it continued to see no real danger.

"Even if...the higher value of the U.S. dollar, which is evident particularly in the mark prices for raw materials and energy products, tends to radiate upward price pressures, this does not necessarily mean that the high level of price stability which has been reached is again in danger," it said.
It added that such factors were offset by low cost increases in the domestic market and the relative sluggishness of the economy.
While moderate wage increases were certainly a positive factor, it would take several years of such developments for this to have any real impact on the jobs market, the Bundesbank said.
Wages also needed to be more sharply differentiated according to region, sector and skills, it added.
